entries.title: The Chat guide suggests where to go next
entries.body: Opening the guide in the Chat panel offers three ways in: "Where should I start?", "Help me work out what I want from this" and "How could I read this well?". After each answer, up to three buttons appear beneath it: a question to ask next, a mode to open, or a search whose words you can edit first. Buttons to share or archive the article take you to its Metadata page and do nothing until you act there.

entries.title: Peer review is renamed Sources
entries.body: The mode that gathers what an article cites, what others say about it and the claims it makes was called Peer review; it is called Sources everywhere. The old name was easy to confuse with Referee, the mode for someone doing a peer review. Old links still open it, and typing "peer review" in the command bar finds it.

entries.title: Refreshing an article's title keeps its other details
entries.body: When we re-read the title and abstract of an article already in the app, details the second pass did not find again, such as the date, DOI, journal and the comparison with the PDF, could disappear from its Metadata page. They are kept, and authors found again keep their affiliations.
